subject: Renewal options: commit retiering and uplift cap clarification
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal proposal & suggested commit tiers for 2027

Hi Lena,

Thanks again for the time on Thursday. Based on your usage profile and the growth signals you shared, attached is a proposed renewal for your Hosted API usage starting Jan 1. Highlights:

- 12-month commit with three tiered per-token thresholds (Base / Mid / High)
- Graduated per-token discounts increasing with usage; overall uplift limited at +20% on committed spend year-over-year
- Option to true-up mid-year if you exceed the High tier (true-up billed at the High-tier price)

I've attached a clean proposal PDF and a short one-pager that maps expected monthly token bands to estimated monthly bills. Please review and tell me which parts you'd like us to tighten up — pricing, uplift cap, or tier thresholds.

Attachments: 2026-11-28-Redwood-proposal-commit-tiers.pdf (proposal), token_bands_onepager.pdf (one-pager)

Best,
Diego
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Diego: +1 415-555-0123

From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal & suggested commit tiers for 2027

Thanks Diego — quick clarifying Qs before I share with procurement: 

1) The proposal references a +20% uplift cap on committed spend YOY. Is that a firm maximum for list-price increases, or can that be adjusted by tier if usage skews into the High band?

2) If we agree to a 12-month commit and then have a big spike, do you allow an intra-year retiering (i.e., move us into the Higher threshold mid-contract) or is our only path a true-up at the end of the quarter?

3) Can you confirm whether the per-token discounts apply to all tokens (generation + context) combined, or only to generated tokens? We need that spelled out for our finance team.

Also: procurement asked if we can cap annual contract uplift to no more than +15% for renewals in the first two years to reduce budget variability. Is that something Redwood can commit to?

Appreciate the details — once I have answers I’ll route to procurement.

Thanks,
Lena
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Analytics

---

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 11:23:00 -0800
Subject: FW: Acme renewal Qs — uplift cap + retiering ask

Team — forwarding Acme's procurement questions (see below). Quick context: Acme is comfortable with the commit volume but procurement is pushing for a lower uplift cap (+15% vs the +20% we proposed) and explicit allowance for mid-year retiering without punitive true-up. Their usage is seasonal and they want to avoid surprise budgets.

Questions for pricing/legal/finance:
- Can we make a customer-facing clause: "annual renewal uplift capped at 15% for the first 24 months"? If not, what is the minimum concession we can offer while protecting ARR?
- Can we formalize an intra-contract retiering policy that allows moving to a higher tier mid-year if they commit to an adjusted minimum spend for the remainder of the term? (We could require a pro-rated commitment top-up.)
- Clarify token definition: do discounts apply to all tokens (input+output) or generation-only? Our standard is both but the contract language usually clarifies.

Putting this on your radar for quick pricing approval — Acme is a mid-size but strategic customer (expanding quickly into our dedicated offering in future).

Thanks,
Diego

Subject: Re: FW: Acme renewal Qs — uplift cap + retiering ask

Diego / Monica — after a quick review with finance: we can agree to a customer amendment with the following guardrails. I cleared this with Karthik and Legal (subject to final contract language):

- Renewal uplift cap: We can lock in a 15% maximum uplift on committed spend for the first 24 months post-renewal. After that period standard pricing policy applies. This should satisfy procurement's risk concern.

- Intra-term retiering: Allow a mid-term retiering option, with the condition that Acme signs a pro-rated top-up to meet the new tier's minimum remaining commitment. The true-up will be calculated pro-rata from the retiering date and billed immediately; ongoing consumption will be billed at the new tier price. This avoids surprise discounts while enabling flexibility.

- Token definition: Confirmed — discounts apply to billable tokens defined as (input tokens + generated tokens) per the proposal appendix. Legal will add the precise language from our billing appendix.

Next steps: Diego, draft a short amendment reflecting these points and send to Acme. Monica, loop in Legal to prepare the amendment doc (use the attached amendment draft as starting point). Karthik — please prepare a one-line CFO approval note for the deal file confirming the 15% cap (we'll need that for procurement).

Marissa
VP Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Renewal proposal & suggested commit tiers for 2027 — agreed amendment

Hi Lena / Acme procurement,

Thanks for the clear questions — we had an internal review and agreed to the following amendment to the proposal (attached: 2026-12-05-Amendment-draft.docx):

- Renewal uplift cap: Redwood will commit to a maximum 15% uplift on committed annual spend for the first 24 months following renewal. This will be expressed as a cap on the renewal price applied to the committed spend in the contract amendment.

- Intra-term retiering: Acme may request a mid-term retiering to a higher threshold. To enact the retiering Acme must sign a pro-rated top-up that increases the remaining committed spend to meet the new tier's minimum; the top-up will be invoiced at the time of retiering. Subsequent usage will be billed at the new tier's per-token prices.

- Token definition: Per the proposal appendix and billing appendix in the amendment, discounts apply to billable tokens (input + generated tokens).

Next steps: I’ve attached the amendment draft for review. If that looks good I’ll route the final amendment to Legal and send a DocuSign for signature. HubSpot deal updated: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567890
